To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in addition to cleaving amyloid precursor protein for β-amyloid production, β-site APP-cleave enzyme 1 (also known as BACE1) interacts with and inhibits adenylate cyclases, resulting in a decrease in cAMP and thus a reduction in the activity of protein kinase A and cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB), a critical regulator for memory functions.
BACE1 regulates the cAMP/PKACREB pathway independently of β-amyloid.
BACE1 regulates the cAMP/PKAc/CREB pathway independently of Aβ production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological role of BACE1, a key enzyme in the pathogenesis of AD.
the regulation of the CREB signaling pathway by BACE1 and its role in memory and learning.
the role of β-secretase BACE1 in the regulation of cAMP/PKA signaling pathway and memory functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data demonstrate that BACE1 regulates CREB phosphorylation via a cAMP-dependent PKA signaling pathway, and the BACE1-mediated regulation of CREB phosphorylation is independent of its function as the Aβ-β-secretase.
our data demonstrate that BACE1 regulates the cAMP/PK/CREB pathway independently of its β-secretase activity.
BACE1 is a novel regulator of the cAMP/PKACREB pathway and its dysregulation may be an additional mechanism by which BACE1 contributes to the pathophysiology of AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in addition to the well-known role of BACE1 in the amyloidogenic pathway for Aβ production (which contributes to the pathophysiology of AD), BACE1 plays a physiological role in regulating the cAMP-PKA-CREB pathway, which may be a novel mechanism for the cognitive deficits in AD.
BACE1 is a multifunctional enzyme and its physiological functions are independent of its activity in generating Aβ.
BACE1, which is the major enzyme for generating Aβ, has an additional role to regulate the cAMP/PKAc/CREB pathway independent of its β-secretase activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BACE1 has multiple functions, and its effect on memory and learning is not necessarily mediated by its ability to generate Aβ.
BACE1 is not just a β-secretase to generate Aβ, but it also regulates the cAMP/PKACREB pathway, which has been linked to memory functions.
BACE1 has multiple physiological functions in addition to its well known function of producing Aβ.
